segments.text: Each AI token starts with a row of numbers called an embedding.
As the AI processes your message,
its layers change those numbers to reflect the surrounding context.
But those new numbers might not match the starting numbers for any existing token.
How can they still represent meaning?
An exact match isn't necessary.
The relationships between the numbers matter too.
We can picture those relationships as positions on a map,
where nearby positions represent similar meanings.
That is the core idea behind vector space.
Looking at this map, we use two numbers to describe a position, latitude and longitude.
Let's add Dallas at 32.78 degrees north, 96.80 degrees west.
Next, Mountain View sits at 37 degrees north, 122 degrees west.
And finally, New York City goes at 41 degrees north, 74 degrees west.
In a simple two-dimensional system like this,
an absolute pair of coordinates locks in an exact location,
giving us a specific defined meaning.
Now, you receive a new set of coordinates that do not match our baseline,
38 degrees north, 120 degrees west.
Which of our three cities is the closest?
The diamond marks the new position,
and the short connection joins it to Mountain View.
Next, try a second mystery coordinate at 40 degrees north, 76 degrees west.
Which city is closest this time?
The new connection identifies New York City as the nearest location.
Though the coordinates didn't match perfectly,
distance calculations allowed us to find the closest match.
A physical map uses two numbers.
We can apply this exact same logic using more than two numbers.
Imagine a taste test where you rate Coke, Pepsi and hot coffee across seven characteristics.
Sweetness, bitterness, fizz, heat, caffeine, darkness, and citrus.
These seven numbers act as abstract coordinates.
Let's plot Coke.
Its coordinates are sweetness nine, bitterness one, fizz ten, heat two,
caffeine three, darkness eight, and citrus one.
Next is Pepsi.
Its coordinates are sweetness nine, bitterness one,
fizz ten, heat two, caffeine three, darkness eight, and citrus ten.
Because Pepsi scores are very close to Coke's,
it drops into the exact same area, forming a soft drinks neighborhood.
Now consider hot coffee.
Its coordinates are sweetness one, bitterness nine, fizz zero,
heat nine, caffeine eight, darkness ten, and citrus zero.
These extreme differences, high bitterness and heat,
zero fizz and citrus, place it far away in its own isolated coffee and tea neighborhood.
While we cannot physically draw all seven dimensions on a flat screen,
projecting them into neighborhoods visually proves which concepts are closest in meaning.
This vector space diagram plots mystery drink A.
Its coordinates are nine, one, ten, two, three, eight, and nine.
Its first six numbers match both Coke and Pepsi exactly.
To find the closest match, we compare the final citrus number.
Mystery drink A is nine, Coke is one, and Pepsi is ten.
Which is closest?
Pepsi is the closest match.
The numerical gap for citrus is only one, compared to a distance of eight for Coke.
Now look at the coffee and tea neighborhood.
We have mystery drink B with scores of two, eight, zero, eight, seven, nine, and zero.
Compare those seven numbers against hot coffee's vector to find the closest match.
Hot coffee is the closest match.
Even though the numbers are not identical, the ratings are highly similar across all seven dimensions.
Comparing those numbers helps us find the closest match,
because smaller numerical gaps mean closer positions.
AI uses this exact distance idea, but with thousands of dimensions learned during training,
meaning a token's updated vector never has to match perfectly to represent meaning.
Context actively changes these numbers.
Take the sentence, the cat sat on the mat during the May rainstorm because it was tired.
On its own, the word it is completely ambiguous.
As the layers process this specific sentence, they update its starting coordinates,
beginning at 0.12, negative 0.34, and shift them to new coordinates, 0.41, 0.06.
This physical change in the numbers moves its position in vector space.
It remains a separate token, but is now near cat.
Its new position reflects its connection to cat in this specific sentence.
Meaning is a position in vector space.
Similar meanings usually sit close together.
